 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparenc  Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (the 2013  Act, for short), the Delhi Development Authority  Signature Not Verified Delhi Development Authority vs Rameshwar Singh Tanwar on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92567104/

sentences.text:
Digitally signed by Indu Marwah Date: 2023.01.31 15:20:32 IST Reason:
 It is the case on behalf of the appellant and so stated  in counter affidavit before the High Court that the land in  2 question was placed under disposal of the respondents under Notification dated 03.01.1968 and the same was transferred to the Engineering department in Kirti Nagar Residential Scheme on 27.12.1976.
It is submitted that it was the case on behalf of the DDA that the compensation with respect to the land in question was deposited with the Reference Court on 16.02.1965.

It is submitted that despite the above, the Honble High Court has allowed the writ petition and declared that the acquisition with respect to the land in question is deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act relying upon the earlier decision of this court in Pune Municipal Corporation &
Anr. Vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki & Ors., reported in 2014 (3)
SCC 183.
 It is submitted that the decision of this Court in the Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr.(supra) has been subsequently overruled in the case of Indore Development Authority Versus Manoharlal &
Ors. Etc.

2  Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and considering the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court, it appears that while passing the impugned judgment and order, the High Court has relied upon the decision of this Court in the case of Pune Municipal Corporation & Anr.(supra) which has been subsequently over-ruled by this Court in the case of Indore  3 Development Authority (supra).

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, the matter is required to be remanded to the High Court for fresh decision of the High Court in accordance with law and on its own merits and in the light of the decision of this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) and or any other subsequent decisions which may be cited.
In view of the above and for the reasons, the present appeal succeeds.

The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court declaring that the acquisition with respect to land in question is deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2) of the 2013 Act is hereby quashed and set aside.

The matter is remitted back to the High Court to decide and dispose of the writ petition afresh in accordance with law and on its own merits and in the light of the law laid down by this Court in the case of Indore Development Authority (supra) and/or any subsequent decisions which may be cited.
The present appeal is accordingly allowed to the aforesaid extent.
No costs.
